_about: Draft answer options for the Should/Will dropdowns (Nov 6). Each case gets 2-4 options; 'meaning' is the one-line explanation in the popup. Threshold questions come first. Not live until approved.

24-1016.label: Question of fact
24-1016.meaning: Trademark strength is decided like other facts, and appeals courts review it deferentially, as twelve circuits do.

24-1016.label: Question of law
24-1016.meaning: Trademark strength is a legal question that appeals courts decide for themselves, as the Second Circuit does.

25-1003.label: Yes
25-1003.meaning: A prisoner can bring a second habeas petition based on a new rule even if a claim based on it could have been raised earlier.

25-1003.label: No
25-1003.meaning: If a claim based on the new rule could have been raised in an earlier petition, the rule wasn't "previously unavailable," and the second petition is barred.

25-1017.label: Arizona wins both
25-1017.meaning: Arizona can require proof of citizenship on its state registration form and can run its citizenship-based removal program close to a federal election.

25-1017.label: Arizona wins proof of citizenship only
25-1017.meaning: Arizona can require proof of citizenship on its state registration form, but can't run its citizenship-based removal program within 90 days of a federal election.

25-1017.label: Arizona wins voter rolls only
25-1017.meaning: Arizona can run its citizenship-based removal program within 90 days of a federal election, but can't require proof of citizenship on its state registration form.

25-1017.label: Arizona loses both
25-1017.meaning: The NVRA or the consent decree blocks both Arizona's proof-of-citizenship requirement and its removal program.

25-1103.label: Yes
25-1103.meaning: The court can order broad discovery against DOGE to decide whether FOIA applies to it.

25-1103.label: No
25-1103.meaning: The court can't order broad discovery against DOGE just to decide whether FOIA applies to it.

25-1131.label: Yes
25-1131.meaning: Barring a religious institution from building a religious structure on its own land substantially burdens religious exercise, so the rule must meet RLUIPA's strict test.

25-1131.label: No
25-1131.meaning: Barring a religious institution from building a religious structure on its own land isn't automatically a substantial burden; the institution has to show more.

25-1223.label: Yes
25-1223.meaning: Noncitizens who win habeas challenges to their immigration detention can recover attorney's fees under EAJA.

25-1223.label: No
25-1223.meaning: Noncitizens who win habeas challenges to their immigration detention can't recover attorney's fees under EAJA.

25-1311.label: Spirit is enough
25-1311.meaning: A court can hold a party in contempt for conduct that undermines an injunction's purpose, even if the injunction doesn't expressly forbid it.

25-1311.label: Clear terms are required
25-1311.meaning: Contempt requires violating an order that clearly and specifically prohibits the conduct.

25-1343.label: Yes
25-1343.meaning: The material-support bar applies only if the support helped the organization carry out terrorism.

25-1343.label: No
25-1343.meaning: Any material support to a terrorist organization—such as cooking meals for the organization's leaders—triggers the bar, even if it didn't advance a terrorist act.

25-1349.label: Yes
25-1349.meaning: State courts can't enforce a divorce agreement's promise to make up the ex-spouse's lost share when retirement pay is replaced by disability pay.

25-1349.label: No
25-1349.meaning: State courts can enforce indemnification promises that the veteran agreed to in a divorce settlement.

25-1408.label: Enforce arbitration
25-1408.meaning: The consumers' automatic-stay claims go to arbitration under their card agreements.

25-1408.label: Bankruptcy court may keep the claims
25-1408.meaning: The bankruptcy court can refuse to send the consumers' automatic-stay claims to arbitration.

25-159.label: Yes
25-159.meaning: Landowners get compensation measured by state law, which is often more generous.

25-159.label: No
25-159.meaning: Landowners get only the minimum compensation the Fifth Amendment requires.

25-170.label: No jurisdiction
25-170.meaning: The Supreme Court can't decide the case, so the Colorado Supreme Court's ruling letting the suit go forward stands.

25-170.label: Jurisdiction; claims precluded
25-170.meaning: Federal law bars Boulder's state-law climate claims, ending the suit.

25-170.label: Jurisdiction; claims may proceed
25-170.meaning: Boulder's state-law climate claims can go forward in Colorado court.

25-183.label: Yes
25-183.meaning: Employees of federally funded schools and universities can sue for sex discrimination under Title IX.

25-183.label: No
25-183.meaning: Employees of federally funded schools and universities can't sue for sex discrimination under Title IX and must rely on other laws, such as Title VII.

25-238.label: Yes
25-238.meaning: The Second Amendment protects possessing AR-15-style rifles, putting bans like Cook County's in doubt.

25-238.label: No
25-238.meaning: The Second Amendment doesn't protect possessing AR-15-style rifles, so bans like Cook County's can stand.

25-246.label: In the abstract
25-246.meaning: Courts may judge how serious the offense is in general terms when deciding whether a forfeiture is excessive.

25-246.label: The owner's specific conduct
25-246.meaning: Courts must look at what the particular owner actually did when deciding whether a forfeiture is excessive.

25-352.label: Yes, even after the amendment deadline
25-352.meaning: A defendant can raise an unpleaded defense at summary judgment without amending, even when the deadline to amend has passed.

25-352.label: Yes, but only before the amendment deadline
25-352.meaning: A defendant can raise an unpleaded defense at summary judgment without amending, but only before the deadline to amend has passed.

25-352.label: No
25-352.meaning: A defendant must amend its answer to include the defense before relying on it.

25-417.label: Yes
25-417.meaning: The prisoner's damages suit can go forward under Bivens.

25-417.label: No
25-417.meaning: Bivens doesn't extend to the prisoner's claim, so the damages suit is dismissed.

25-459.label: All goods and services
25-459.meaning: A newsletter subscriber can be a protected "consumer," so sharing his video-viewing history can create liability under the VPPA.

25-459.label: Only audiovisual goods and services
25-459.meaning: Only subscribers to video goods or services count, so a newsletter subscriber isn't protected under the VPPA.

25-498.label: Yes, a benchmark is required
25-498.meaning: Plaintiffs claiming imprudent investing based on poor returns must point to a comparable investment that did better.

25-498.label: No benchmark required
25-498.meaning: Plaintiffs can state a claim without a specific comparison, based on the circumstances as a whole.

25-5343.label: Yes
25-5343.meaning: Courts keep giving the Sentencing Commission's commentary strong deference under Stinson.

25-5343.label: No
25-5343.meaning: Stinson's rule is replaced, and courts give the Sentencing Commission's commentary less weight.

25-566.label: Yes
25-566.meaning: The Second Amendment protects possessing AR-15-style rifles, putting bans like Connecticut's in doubt.

25-566.label: No
25-566.meaning: The Second Amendment doesn't protect possessing AR-15-style rifles, so bans like Connecticut's can stand.

25-579.label: Not reviewable yet
25-579.meaning: The Air Force's submission of its permit-renewal application isn't final agency action, so it can't be challenged now.

25-579.label: Reviewable; NEPA not required
25-579.meaning: The Air Force's permit-renewal application can be challenged now, but it doesn't need NEPA review because RCRA has its own procedures.

25-579.label: Reviewable; NEPA required
25-579.meaning: The Air Force's permit-renewal application can be challenged now, and the Air Force must complete NEPA review before applying.

25-581.label: St. Mary wins both
25-581.meaning: Colorado's rule fails both tests, so excluding the Catholic preschools faces strict scrutiny.

25-581.label: St. Mary wins on general applicability only
25-581.meaning: Colorado's exemptions make its preschool rule not generally applicable, but the rule against excluding religious institutions from public benefits doesn't apply.

25-581.label: St. Mary wins on public benefits only
25-581.meaning: The rule against excluding religious institutions from public benefits applies, but Colorado's preschool rule still counts as generally applicable.

25-581.label: Colorado wins both
25-581.meaning: Colorado can exclude the Catholic preschools.

25-5930.label: Yes
25-5930.meaning: Prisoners can use habeas to challenge how First Step Act time credits affect their transfer to a halfway house or home confinement.

25-5930.label: No
25-5930.meaning: Prisoners must bring challenges to First Step Act time credits another way, such as a civil-rights suit.

25-6623.label: Yes
25-6623.meaning: Defendants charged with serious felonies are entitled to 12-person juries, so Florida's six-person felony juries are unconstitutional.

25-6623.label: No
25-6623.meaning: States may keep using smaller juries in felony trials.

25-7026.label: Yes
25-7026.meaning: When circuits disagree, a prisoner gets permission to appeal even if their own circuit's precedent is against them.

25-7026.label: No
25-7026.meaning: Binding circuit precedent against the prisoner is enough to deny permission to appeal.

25-735.label: Yes
25-735.meaning: Veterans can't bring constitutional challenges to laws affecting veterans' benefits in district court and must go through the veterans' benefits review system.

25-735.label: No
25-735.meaning: District courts can still hear constitutional challenges to laws affecting veterans' benefits.

25-840.label: Yes
25-840.meaning: The parents can challenge Washington's law in federal court.

25-840.label: No
25-840.meaning: The parents lack standing to challenge Washington's law, so the suit is dismissed without a ruling on the law itself.

25-842.label: Eligible
25-842.meaning: People whose asylum was terminated can still seek permanent residence if they meet the other requirements.

25-842.label: Categorically ineligible
25-842.meaning: Termination of asylum ends the path to permanent residence through asylum.

25-965.label: Yes
25-965.meaning: The plaintiff can sue over chilling threats from a city government even without waiting for a final land-use decision.

25-965.label: No
25-965.meaning: The plaintiff cannot sue over chilling threats from a city government until the city completes a final land-use decision.

25-966.label: Labor Department wins both
25-966.meaning: The Department can keep deciding these H-2A penalty cases itself.

25-966.label: The INA doesn't authorize it
25-966.meaning: The INA doesn't give the Labor Department power to decide these H-2A penalty cases, so they must go to court.

25-966.label: Article III bars it
25-966.meaning: Even if the INA authorizes the Labor Department to decide these H-2A penalty cases, the Constitution requires a federal court to decide them.

26-104.label: Yes
26-104.meaning: People who entered without being admitted must be detained while their removal cases proceed, without bond hearings.

26-104.label: No
26-104.meaning: People who entered without being admitted aren't subject to mandatory detention and may seek release on bond.

26-12.label: Yes
26-12.meaning: A challenge fails unless the targeted group, overall, fared worse relative to its share of applicants.

26-12.label: No
26-12.meaning: Evidence of discriminatory intent can support a challenge even without that overall statistical showing.

26-204.label: Yes
26-204.meaning: The ban on home distilling is a valid exercise of Congress's taxing power.

26-204.label: No
26-204.meaning: Congress lacks the power to ban home distilling this way.

26-426.label: No jurisdiction
26-426.meaning: The district court couldn't hear the challenge, so its judgment is undone.

26-426.label: Jurisdiction; no classwide relief
26-426.meaning: The district court could hear the challenge but couldn't grant classwide relief or set aside the guidance.

26-426.label: Classwide relief allowed; guidance lawful
26-426.meaning: The district court could grant classwide relief, but the government's third-country removal guidance is lawful.

26-426.label: Classwide relief allowed; guidance unlawful
26-426.meaning: The district court's judgment setting aside the government's third-country removal guidance stands.
